Worksheet 2 | HL Synthesis

Build the House Competition Database

This is the optional synthesis worksheet. Start from a blank workspace, build the database from the schema and ERD, batch-load the starter rows, and then use HL aggregate functions to produce competition reports.

CREATE TABLE INSERT COUNT AVG SUM HAVING
Open Blank Workspace All HL SQL worksheets

Build Goal

  • Create a four-table reporting database from scratch
  • Use a composite key in the results table
  • Finish with grouped reporting queries

Syllabus Links

  • SL structure work: keys, relationships, DDL, and batch inserts
  • HL extension: COUNT, AVG, SUM, MAX, MIN, GROUP BY, and HAVING
  • One synthesis task instead of another preloaded practice sheet

Before You Start

  • Use the blank workspace, not the course enrolment dataset.
  • Create the parent tables before the child tables.
  • Get the structure correct before you run the aggregate queries.
1

Blueprint

Use this schema and ERD as the design brief for the database you are about to build.

HOUSE

  • HouseIDTEXT PK
  • HouseNameTEXT
  • StaffLeadTEXT

EVENT

  • EventIDINTEGER PK
  • EventNameTEXT
  • CategoryTEXT

STUDENT

  • StudentIDINTEGER PK
  • FirstNameTEXT
  • LastNameTEXT
  • HouseIDTEXT FK

RESULT

  • StudentIDINTEGER FK
  • EventIDINTEGER FK
  • ScoreINTEGER
  • PositionINTEGER
  • Primary key(StudentID, EventID)
  1. A3.2.4 Build order

    Write down the order in which the four tables should be created so the foreign keys can be added without errors.

  2. A3.2.4 Composite key

    Explain why RESULT needs a composite primary key rather than a single field from the schema above.

2

Create the Tables

Build the structure first, then load the data.

Reference pattern — CREATE TABLE for reporting databases 
CREATE TABLE parent_table (
    parent_id   TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    label_text  TEXT
);

CREATE TABLE child_table (
    child_id    INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    parent_id   TEXT,
    value_text  TEXT,
    FOREIGN KEY (parent_id) REFERENCES parent_table(parent_id)
);

CREATE TABLE result_table (
    first_id    INTEGER,
    second_id   INTEGER,
    score_value INTEGER,
    PRIMARY KEY (first_id, second_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (first_id) REFERENCES first_table(first_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (second_id) REFERENCES second_table(second_id)
);

A reporting table often combines two foreign keys into one composite key so each relationship appears only once.

  1. A3.3.1 DDL

    Create HOUSE and EVENT first.

  2. A3.3.1 Foreign key

    Create STUDENT with a foreign key back to HOUSE.

  3. A3.3.1 Composite key

    Create RESULT with the composite primary key (StudentID, EventID) plus both foreign keys.

3

Load the Starter Data

Use multi-row inserts so the build does not become a typing exercise.

Reference pattern — batch INSERT 
INSERT INTO table_name (column_a, column_b, column_c)
VALUES
    ('A', 'First row', 10),
    ('B', 'Second row', 20),
    ('C', 'Third row', 30);

INSERT INTO result_table (first_id, second_id, score_value, rank_value)
VALUES
    (101, 501, 18, 1),
    (102, 501, 16, 2),
    (103, 501, 14, 3);

One statement can add several rows. That keeps the worksheet focused on the database logic, not repetitive typing.

4

Aggregate Reports

Use the database you built to answer grouped-report questions.

Reference pattern — aggregate reporting 
SELECT category_column, COUNT(*) AS item_count
FROM table_name
GROUP BY category_column;

SELECT category_column, ROUND(AVG(score_column), 1) AS average_score
FROM table_name
GROUP BY category_column;

SELECT category_column, SUM(score_column) AS total_score
FROM table_name
GROUP BY category_column
HAVING SUM(score_column) >= 30;

Once the schema and rows are correct, the HL part is the reporting: choose the right group, the right aggregate function, and the right threshold.

  1. A3.3.4 COUNT

    Count how many result rows each event has.

  2. A3.3.4 AVG

    Calculate the average score for each event.

  3. A3.3.4 SUM

    Sum the total score for each house by joining HOUSE, STUDENT, and RESULT.

  4. A3.3.4 MAX / MIN

    Return the highest and lowest score in each event.

  5. A3.3.4 HAVING

    Show only houses with at least 3 recorded results.

  6. A3.3.4 Report query

    Produce a house report showing house name, result count, total score, and rounded average score, ordered from highest total score to lowest.

Teacher Answers

Enter the teacher password to reveal model answers for this worksheet.

Model Answers — Build the House Competition Database

Section 1

1
Recommended table order Create HOUSE and EVENT first, then STUDENT, then RESULT. The composite key (StudentID, EventID) prevents duplicate result rows for the same student-event pair.

Section 2

2
Core DDL pattern 
CREATE TABLE HOUSE (
    HouseID TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    HouseName TEXT,
    StaffLead TEXT
);

CREATE TABLE EVENT (
    EventID INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    EventName TEXT,
    Category TEXT
);

CREATE TABLE STUDENT (
    StudentID INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    FirstName TEXT,
    LastName TEXT,
    HouseID TEXT,
    FOREIGN KEY (HouseID) REFERENCES HOUSE(HouseID)
);

CREATE TABLE RESULT (
    StudentID INTEGER,
    EventID INTEGER,
    Score INTEGER,
    Position INTEGER,
    PRIMARY KEY (StudentID, EventID),
    FOREIGN KEY (StudentID) REFERENCES STUDENT(StudentID),
    FOREIGN KEY (EventID) REFERENCES EVENT(EventID)
);

Section 4

3
House report example 
SELECT h.HouseName,
       COUNT(*) AS ResultCount,
       SUM(r.Score) AS TotalScore,
       ROUND(AVG(r.Score), 1) AS AverageScore
FROM RESULT AS r
JOIN STUDENT AS s
    ON r.StudentID = s.StudentID
JOIN HOUSE AS h
    ON s.HouseID = h.HouseID
GROUP BY h.HouseName
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3
ORDER BY TotalScore DESC, h.HouseName;
